newsitem.title: USA: Only few Cerro traders taken on by MG - source.
newsitem.headline: Only few Cerro traders taken on by MG - source.

text.p: Cerro Sales Corp of New York ceases trading at the end of May with fewer than half of its dealers going to MG Metal & Commodity Group, part of Germany's Metallgesellschaft, a source close to the deal said.
Officials at MG in New York were not immediately available for comment.
COMEX copper floor sources said liquidation of Cerro positions was dampening prices Wednesday and causing aberrations in arbitrage which will probably last another day or two.
MG announced at the end of April it was buying Cerro Sales Corp, part of privately held Marmon Group. Closure of the deal was due late May.
The source said six to eight people would probably be taken on by MG in New York out of the 20 or so staff at Cerro.

Those not taken on by MG and with no job elsewhere, will be laid off at the end of June. "Technically they close the end of May, but they will keep people on until the end of June to tie up some loose ends," the source added.

MG and Cerro are major arbitrage dealers in COMEX copper, and some traders fear that Cerro's exit will harm liquidity on the New York exchange which is trying to boost volumes in the face of LME rivalry.
